result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

result.rule: When the description presents alternative ways to initiate a process that lead to the same subsequent handling: Represent the alternatives with an exclusive gateway and converge them before the shared handling; do not invent channel-specific work.

When the description says an activity may occur in addition to the main sequence: Model the activity on an optional path, using a decision gateway to determine whether it occurs, and rejoin the main sequence afterward.

When the description says that a later activity proceeds only after approval or another decision: Model the described preceding action and approval step in order, then use an exclusive gateway to route the approved path to the dependent activity.

When the description names alternative actions that can each signal or cause the same subsequent step: model each stated alternative as a distinct activity or event and preserve its path to the shared step, rather than omitting an alternative or substituting a different action
